function_v0.doc:
CHANGED T2/D1: `deadline` + `signature` are now required arguments.
When `caller` is the oracle the contract verifies an Ed25519
signature over the verdict on-chain; when `caller` is the admin
(manual fallback) both are ignored, exactly as in V8. See
`claim::submit_claim` for the full auth-model rationale.
function_v0.name: submit_claim

function_v0.doc:
Deploy-time initialization.

CHANGED 2026-08-17 (7a audit, Finding 3): was a separate `initialize`
entrypoint. Renamed to `__constructor`, the SDK-recognised constructor
hook, which runs **as part of the deploy invocation itself**.

Why this mattered: `initialize` authorized the `admin` **argument**
passed to it, and the only thing stopping a second call was the
`AlreadyInitialized` guard. That guard protects against
re-initialization but not against being *first*, between the deploy
transaction and the legitimate init transaction, anyone observing the
chain could call `initialize` with themselves as admin and satisfy
`require_auth` trivially. The T1 testnet deployment used two separate
transactions (README), so the window was real rather than theoretical.
Stellar's own guidance is explicit: prefer `__constructor` because it
"removes the front-running window between deploy and init", and note
that a contract deployed without one can never gain it afterwards,
which is why this had to change before D4's deploy,
function_v0.name: __constructor

function_v0.doc:

fields.doc:
NEW 2026-07-22 (Rule A): set when entering `AwaitingApproval`
(`now + APPROVE_WINDOW_LEDGERS`). Checked by both `approve_claim`
(must call before this) and the permissionless `expire_pending_approval`
(may sweep after this). Unused (0) before that state is reached.
fields.name: approve_deadline_ledger

fields.doc: Total approved payout.
fields.name: entitlement

fields.doc: Ledger timestamp of the hack event, validated at submit_claim.
fields.name: hack_timestamp

fields.doc:
NEW 2026-07-22 (Rule B): set to `cooldown_ends_ledger`, not the
approval ledger: the moment a claim activates (eng review blocker
#2: the mandatory 7-day cooldown must never count as staker
inactivity). Updated to `now` on every successful `claim_stream`.
Checked by the permissionless `expire_stale_claim`. Unused (0)
before activation.
fields.name: last_collected_ledger

fields.doc: Stake amount captured at submit_claim, used by cancel_claim to\nrestore total_staked on a false-positive reversal.
fields.name: stake

fields.doc: Already streamed to the beneficiary so far.
fields.name: streamed

fields.doc: Assessed by the oracle at claim time, included in its signed\nverdict: never re-derivable/forgeable client-side.
fields.name: tier

fields.doc:
CORRECTED 2026-07-14 (second pass, full source read): NOT "fixed at
end of cooldown" as an earlier note claimed. Activation happens
synchronously: either inside submit_claim itself (gate already
met) or inside unlock_pending_claim (gate met later), and
cooldown_ends/vesting_ends are set as FUTURE deadlines starting
from that same activation moment, not preconditions for it. The
snapshot is total_staked read immediately before THIS claim's own
forfeiture decrement, in that same call. Still matters for the
same reason: get the timing wrong and the outflow cap's
anti-manipulation guarantee breaks.
v1 (2026-09-22): now snapshots CAPACITY (`total_staked +
total_backed`), not staker principal alone. Field name kept: struct
field names are part of the stored XDR.
fields.name: total_staked_snapshot

cases.doc:
NEW 2026-07-22 (Rule A): 90-day gate met, reservation live, nothing
forfeited yet: waiting on the staker's own `approve_claim` call
within `APPROVE_WINDOW_LEDGERS`. Replaces the old behavior where
meeting the time gate auto-forfeited the stake with no staker
action required.
cases.name: AwaitingApproval

cases.doc:
NEW 2026-07-22: terminal state for a reservation that lapsed
without staker action: either Rule A (never approved in time) or
Rule B (approved, then went inactive too long during collection).
Same downstream handling either way: release whatever's still
reserved, stop further action. Distinct from `Cancelled`, which
implies an admin false-positive judgment call and its associated
penalty-lock logic: an expiry is neither party's fault.
cases.name: Expired

fields.doc:
CHANGED 2026-07-22 (eng review, bug 2 fix): was a bare `claim_active:
bool`. A bool alone can't distinguish "re-executing/correcting THIS
SAME claim" from "wallet already has a DIFFERENT claim in flight",
`execute_override` needs that distinction to enforce the one-wallet-
one-claim invariant, which a bool structurally cannot express.
`Some(claim_id)` while any claim is open against this stake (blocks
withdrawal, same as the old bool); `None` once terminal
(Completed/Cancelled/Expired) or never claimed.
fields.name: active_claim_id

fields.doc:
sha256(beneficiary), plaintext beneficiary address is never stored.
Decided 2026-07-14: sha256 not keccak256 (Soroban-native, consistent
with the Ed25519 oracle-auth decision; no cross-chain hash-matching
requirement exists for this field).
fields.name: beneficiary_hash

fields.doc: Pre-audit hardening (2026-09-23): set when a claim on this stake is\napproved (the stake is forfeited). The address can never stake again\n(pool rule). Cleared only by `cancel_claim` undoing that claim.
fields.name: claim_approved

fields.doc: Set by cancel_claim on a false-positive reversal; blocks withdraw\nfor PENALTY_LOCK_LEDGERS. 0 if never penalized.
fields.name: penalty_locked_until_ledger

fields.doc:
T3 (2026-08-24): `Some(claim_id)` while a `submit_claim` for this
wallet is sitting in `ClaimStatus::Reserved` (rejected for
`DailyStressCapExceeded`/`Insolvent`, not yet released or expired).
Deliberately separate from `active_claim_id`: a Reserved claim
isn't "active" (it holds no capacity reservation: `total_allocated`
is untouched until release), but the wallet still can't queue a
second one without this guard.
fields.name: reserved_claim_id

fields.doc:
Real Unix timestamp at stake time, used ONLY for the absolute
hack_timestamp sanity check in submit_claim ("hack can't predate
the stake"). staked_at_ledger remains the source of truth for all
duration/gate math (time gate, cooldown, vesting, penalty lock).
fields.name: staked_at_timestamp

fields.doc: Admin can block payout eligibility; does NOT block principal withdrawal.
fields.name: suspended

fields.doc:
`YieldIndex` at the moment this stake was created. `withdraw()`
computes the payout as `amount * current_index / yield_index_at_stake`.
This is the snapshot half of that ratio, so a staker only accrues
yield realised AFTER they joined, never retroactively. Fresh stakes
on a pool that has never realised yield snapshot at
`YIELD_INDEX_PRECISION` (the 1.0x starting value), so the ratio is
exactly 1 until the first `extract_yield` call.

r3 (2026-09-29): the index is ADDITIVE per unit of principal (each
credit adds `share * PRECISION / total_staked`), so yield owed is
`amount * (YieldIndex - yield_index_at_stake) / PRECISION`. The old
ratio `amount * index / at_stake` underpaid anyone who joined after
the first credit. Reset to the live index whenever yield is paid out.
fields.name: yield_index_at_stake

fields.doc: Matured money: counts toward capacity, can be requested out.
fields.name: amount

fields.doc: Deposited but not yet matured: held, does NOT count toward capacity.
fields.name: pending_amount

fields.doc: Timestamp at which `pending_amount` matures; 0 when nothing pending.
fields.name: pending_matures_at

fields.doc: Open withdrawal request (0 = none). Still counted toward capacity\nuntil completed (rule 2).
fields.name: withdraw_amount

fields.doc: Earliest completion timestamp for the open request.
fields.name: withdraw_ready_at

fields.doc: r3: `BackerYieldIndex` at the last settlement of this record.
fields.name: yield_index_at

fields.doc: r3: yield settled to this backer and not yet paid.
fields.name: yield_owed

fields.doc:
The actual approving address, not a bare bool, found via
adversarial review (2026-07-14, Solodit "operator retains power
after removal" pattern class): a bool can't tell a CURRENT
admin/coSigner's approval apart from a STALE one left over from
before a set_co_signer/transfer_admin rotation. Readiness is
derived by comparing these against the CURRENT admin/coSigner at
execution time, so a rotation automatically invalidates an old
approval instead of letting it silently carry forward.
fields.name: owner_approver

event_v0.doc: r3: a staker's or backer's yield paid out.
event_v0.name: YieldPaid

event_v0.doc: r3 (2026-09-29): emitted every time vault growth is recognised as yield,\nwhichever path redeemed it (harvest, in-path pull, keeper, admin).\nReplaces `YieldExtracted`. Nothing transfers here.
event_v0.name: YieldCredited

event_v0.doc: v1 (2026-09-24): an in-path push got fewer shares than the contract's\nown reference rate allows. The shares actually received are recorded\n(accounting stays true, design decision A); this makes it visible.
event_v0.name: PushBelowFloor

event_v0.doc:
Emitted when a redemption returns LESS XLM than the proportional
principal that was deployed: i.e. the venue lost money (Blend bad debt
or an adverse share-price move).

V8 has no equivalent. Its `extractYield` handles the same case only by
declining to extract (`:912`, `receivedEth > ethEquiv ? ... : 0`), so a
principal shortfall is silently absorbed and only surfaces much later as
an inability to pay a claim. Emitting a distinct event costs nothing and
turns a silent loss into something monitorable off-chain. The full
remedy is T3 scope; this is the cheap detection half.
event_v0.name: DeploymentShortfall

event_v0.doc: T3 (2026-08-24), `auto_deploy_liquidity`'s permissionless-triggered\npush, the deposit-side mirror of `LiquidityAutoRebalanced`.
event_v0.name: LiquidityAutoDeployed

event_v0.doc: T3 (2026-08-24), `ensure_liquidity`'s permissionless-triggered pull.\nDistinct from `LiquidityProvided` so on-chain monitoring can tell an\nautomatic rebalance apart from an admin's manual `provide_liquidity`.
event_v0.name: LiquidityAutoRebalanced

void_v0.doc:
D1 (T2): the oracle's Ed25519 ATTESTATION identity, stored ALONGSIDE
`Oracle` (the policy identity), deliberately not a replacement.

The two are not interchangeable and each is load-bearing somewhere
the other cannot serve. `Oracle: Address` is read by the oracle-only
daily claim rate limit (claim.rs), `stake.rs`'s `BeneficiaryIsOracle`
guard, and admin's `OracleEqualsCoSigner`/`CoSignerEqualsOracle`
invariants: a `BytesN<32>` cannot be compared against a beneficiary
`Address`, and a contract-type oracle address has no ed25519 pubkey
at all. `OraclePubKey` is what `ed25519_verify` needs and an Address
cannot supply. Swapping one for the other breaks working code for
zero benefit; the cost of keeping both is a few bytes.
void_v0.name: OraclePubKey

void_v0.doc:
Configurable pool cap (V8: `maxPoolSize`), admin-adjustable up to
whatever hard ceiling the deployment chooses. Per-staker min/max
stake is computed live from this value \xc3\x97 MIN_STAKE_BPS/MAX_STAKE_BPS
(types.rs), so bounds never need re-anchoring when the cap changes.
void_v0.name: PoolCap

void_v0.doc:
Aave-style growing multiplier for staker yield share. Starts at
YIELD_INDEX_PRECISION (1.0x) and only ever increases, at
`extract_yield` time. A stake's withdrawable value is
`amount * YieldIndex / yield_index_at_stake`.
void_v0.name: YieldIndex

void_v0.doc:
Protocol's realised, unwithdrawn yield share, explicit
increment/decrement bookkeeping, NOT computed as a residual. The
old `yield_balance()` residual formula had a documented real bug
(2026-08-20: two activated claims misread as +4,100 XLM "yield");
an explicit counter cannot drift the same way.
void_v0.name: ProtocolYieldBalance

void_v0.doc: Staker COUNT, separate from TotalStaked (the amount). V8: totalStakers.\nMissing from the first two build passes, found on full source read.
void_v0.name: TotalStakers

void_v0.doc:
Admission-side daily cap tracking (submit_claim), separate from the
payout-side DailyOutflow/LastOutflowDay (claim_stream) above. V8 uses
three parallel instance vars (dailyEntitlementTotal/lastEntitlementDay/
dailyClaimCount) with the same day-rollover pattern, not a per-day
keyed counter: corrected here after an earlier draft built the wrong
mechanism (a temporary-storage ClaimAdmissionCount(u32) key that
tracked count only, not the entitlement sum, and didn't match V8's
reset semantics).
void_v0.name: DailyEntitlementTotal

void_v0.doc:
D2 (T2): DeFindex vault address. Deliberately NOT an `initialize`
argument and never accepted as a function parameter on any
user-facing path (Soroban vuln checklist #9, an attacker-suppliable
external contract address is an arbitrary-call primitive). Unset
until admin calls `set_vault`, which is why the whole yield layer is
fail-closed on a fresh deploy.
void_v0.name: Vault

void_v0.doc: D2: destination for extracted yield. V8: `treasuryWallet`.
void_v0.name: Treasury

void_v0.doc: D2: max fraction of `total_staked` deployable, in bps. Unset reads\nas 0, so nothing can be deployed until admin opts in.
void_v0.name: DeployBps

void_v0.doc:
D2: vault shares (dfTokens) this contract holds. V8: `totalDeployed`
(wstETH units). Tracked locally rather than read from
`vault.balance()` at decision time so the accounting stays a pure
internal number: see `TotalDeployedAsset` for why that matters.
void_v0.name: TotalDeployedShares

void_v0.doc:
D2: XLM deployed, valued at ORIGINAL DEPOSIT VALUE, never marked to
market. V8: `totalDeployedETH`, "ETH equivalent deployed to Lido
(original stake amounts)" (`SAFUPoolV8.sol:137`).

This convention is what keeps replays deterministic. The vault's
share price is an externally mutable value that drifts between
transactions; marking to market would drag it into the solvency
invariant and reintroduce exactly the hazard the scanner's
reputation-feed pinning rule exists to prevent. Held at original
value, this stays a pure accounting figure and no externally
mutable value feeds any payout decision at all.
void_v0.name: TotalDeployedAsset

void_v0.doc: D2: running sum of XLM sent to treasury. V8: `totalExtractedYield`.
void_v0.name: TotalExtractedYield

tuple_v0.doc: Banked points after stake exit, accumulates across all cycles. V8:\npointsBalance. Missing from the first two build passes.
tuple_v0.name: PointsBalance

tuple_v0.doc:
D1 (T2): keyed by the sha256 of the approval payload, the direct
analogue of V8's `revokedApprovals[keccak256(inner)]`. Lives in
`temporary()` rather than `persistent()`: a revocation is only
meaningful until the approval's own `deadline` passes, after which
`SignatureExpired` rejects that approval regardless. See
`types::REVOCATION_TTL_LEDGERS` for why expiry here is safe.
tuple_v0.name: RevokedApproval

tuple_v0.doc: v1 (2026-09-22): an adjustable setting's live value, once changed\nfrom its default (settings.rs). Instance storage: a small, fixed set.
tuple_v0.name: Setting

tuple_v0.doc: v1: a proposed setting change awaiting approval / its timelock.
tuple_v0.name: PendingSetting

void_v0.doc: v1 (2026-09-22, backer.rs): matured backer money, counts toward\ncapacity. Instance.
void_v0.name: TotalBacked

void_v0.doc: v1: deposited backer money not yet matured, does NOT count. Instance.

void_v0.doc: Pre-audit hardening (2026-09-23): the third governance role.
void_v0.name: Guardian

void_v0.doc: Timestamp a pause ends (0 = not paused). Replaces `Paused`.
void_v0.name: PausedUntil

tuple_v0.doc: A pending governance change, one slot per kind (governance.rs).
tuple_v0.name: GovPending

void_v0.doc: r3 (2026-09-29): growing multiplier for backer yield, same shape as\n`YieldIndex` but over matured backer money (`TotalBacked`).
void_v0.name: BackerYieldIndex

void_v0.doc: r3: staker yield credited but not yet paid. Held as cash in the pool\nand set aside: never deployed, never used for claims or principal.

void_v0.doc: r3: backer yield credited but not yet paid. Same rule as above.

void_v0.doc: r3: set on the first stake or first backing, never cleared. Until\nthen, vault / treasury / deploy-ceiling changes need no 7-day wait.

void_v0.doc: r3 (CSO M2): time of the last successful harvest (the growth limit's clock).
void_v0.name: LastHarvestAt
